art.subject: Grey-sided Thrush (Turdus feae), adult male in spring: upperparts warm rufescent olive-brown from crown to tail; a white supercilium and a white crescent below the eye; dark lores; chin and throat white; breast and flanks plain grey; centre of the belly and undertail coverts white; wings and tail olive-brown; bill bright yellow with a dusky ridge and tip to the upper mandible; dark eye; yellowish-orange legs.
art.pose: standing on the forest floor among leaf litter, side view
art.scene: deciduous woodland floor on a Korean offshore island in May, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view standing on leaf litter: rufescent olive-brown crown, ear-coverts, back, wings and tail, white supercilium, white crescent below the eye, whitish throat, plain grey breast and flanks paling to whitish on the belly and vent, yellow bill with a dark tip, yellowish legs

adult male, front three-quarter view standing: olive-brown head with a white supercilium and a white crescent below the eye, whitish throat, plain unspotted grey breast and flanks, whitish belly centre, yellow bill
art.build: A medium-sized thrush, smaller and slimmer than a Dusky Thrush and very like an Eyebrowed Thrush in size and shape, with a rounded head and no crest. Bill straight, slightly shorter than the head, mostly yellow. Legs medium, yellowish-orange. Tail medium, square, plain. Shy, feeding on the ground in forest.
avoid: Do not paint orange flanks; that is Eyebrowed Thrush (Turdus obscurus). This species has a grey breast and flanks.
Do not paint a grey head; the crown and face are olive-brown with a white supercilium.
Do not spot or streak the underparts.
Do not paint a dark bill or brown legs; the bill is mostly yellow and the legs yellowish-orange.
